text:
The Athletic ran a long piece this week on Luke Hughes shedding his brothers' shadows, and the season backs up the headline. The youngest Hughes is playing more than 24 minutes a night for New Jersey, the most of his career by a distance, and has 6 goals and 14 points in 22 games. Those 6 goals already match his total from all of last season.

The offense is the real thing. He's in the top 3% of the league in bursts over 20 mph, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him carrying the puck in and getting to the slot more than most defensemen last season. His goals are running a little ahead of his chances (6 on 3.8 expected), so some of the pace is luck.

The question has always been the other end. Evolving-Hockey had him in the bottom 3% of defensemen at preventing chances last season, and this year the Devils are about two points worse in expected goals share with him on at five on five than when he sits, even though they control play overall. We'd watch that number. If it climbs, the breakout is complete.
